comparator.name: Religious Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: Leiden changed the Religious Studies curriculum from 1 September 2026. The current study guide and programme-specific regulations establish the revised 60-EC first year for students entering in 2026-2027. The displayed second year is explicitly for students who entered in 2025-2026, and the published third year belongs to the earlier curriculum sequence. The regulations' transitional provisions likewise specify a second-year programme for students who entered in 2025-2026 or earlier. Combining the new first year with those transition-cohort later years would invent an unconfirmed pathway. The supported current-entry components below therefore retain only the published revised first year.

components.name: Introduction to the Study of Islam
Methods and Techniques 1: Source-Based Research, Objects and Texts
Core Curriculum: Humanities in a Digital World

exception.reason: Current official 2026-2027 sources establish the complete revised 60-EC first year for a new Religious Studies entrant but do not publish that cohort's second- or third-year curriculum. The later-year material currently displayed is identified for transition cohorts. A coherent 180-EC current-entry comparator cannot therefore be certified without mixing different curriculum generations.
exception.curriculumContext: The supported revised first year introduces Religious Studies; Islam, Hindu religions, Christianity and religions of antiquity; religion in a global comparative frame; anthropology of religion; source-, object- and text-based research; qualitative field research; and the faculty digital-humanities core. The official programme description confirms that later study is intended to extend research training through psychology, sociology, comparative work, electives and a bachelor thesis, but the current sources do not yet specify the remaining 120 EC for the 2026 entrant cohort. Revisit when Leiden publishes the revised second and third years.
